A nominal Fe35Ni35Cr20Mn10 (in at. %) HEA was prepared in a vacuum-induction furnace using high-purity (HP; > 99.5wt.%) metals. Each ingot obtained weighed approximately 10 kg.
The ingot was first repeatedly hot-forged at 900-800 °C into a slab
and then homogenization-annealed at 1000 °C for 12 h
Then, the slab was cut into 170 9 21 9 16 mm3 cuboids by wire-cutting and free-forged (at 900-800 °C) into 7 mm diameter rods.
Before drawing, each rod was shaped to a diameter of 6.34 mm by rotary swaging at room temperature
and then annealed at 900 °C for 1 h

attributes.morphology: elongated layers along the drawing direction
attributes.note: approximately 97.57% of the total grains were deformed

evidence.quote: Grains in the as-drawn sample underwent severe plastic deformation along the drawing direction and exhibit a multilayer structure. Approximately 97.57% of the total grains were deformed, as shown in Fig. 2(a).

In the early stage of drawing, the dislocation slipping systems of Fe35Ni35Cr20Mn10 HEA are activated, which induces the accumulation, entanglement, and proliferation of dislocations and results in the formation of dislocation substructures (dislocation cells or walls).

attributes.note: high dislocation density in as-drawn state

evidence.quote: The wire in the as-drawn state exhibited the highest strength but the lowest elongation because of its fine multilayer structure and high dislocation density.
The fractions of SGBs, LAGBs, and HAGBs were 34.61, 24.44, and 40.95%, respectively, and the fraction of deformation TBs was 2.51%.

Increasing the annealing temperature significantly decreased the dislocation density, notably coarsened the recrystallized grains, and significantly increased the fraction of twin boundaries and mean widths of annealing twins.
In addition to the decrease in dislocation density, the formation of annealing twins played an important role in enhancing the elongation.
